BeforeSideTurnEnd.issue: Rollup of guards G1 and G2 per binding rule 4. The arithmetic, the empty-hand guard and the Unpowered prop all match, and the slot is correctly ahead of the hand flush -- but the sim has no sub-phase ordering inside its turn-end walk (G1) and no AutoPostPlay phase before it (G2), so the hand this relic counts can differ from the hand the game counts.

guards.what: G1 (LIVE): the BeforeSideTurnEndVeryEarly / Early / plain sub-phases are flattened into one listener walk, and Cloak Clasp is the named witness
guards.issue: Closed 2026-07-27: the phase passes are real. `HookSystem._each` walks the four phases very_early -> early -> plain -> late as COMPLETE separate listener passes whenever any current listener declares a phase variant of that hook (sts2_rl/hooks.py:36-38, 153-180), which is what Hook.cs's 24 multi-pass dispatchers do. The witness this entry names is settled at its own site: relic/orichalcum now snapshots `Block > 0` from `on_player_turn_end_very_early`, a complete pass that precedes every plain-phase listener, so Cloak Clasp's plain-phase block grant can no longer beat it to the read. WAS: one flat pass, so [cloak_clasp, orichalcum] gave 5 Block and the reverse order 11.

guards.what: G2 (LIVE): the AutoPostPlay phase does not exist, so end-of-turn auto-plays that C# runs BEFORE this relic can run after it
guards.rationale: CombatManager.cs:1160-1176 (read today) sets `player.PlayerCombatState.Phase = PlayerTurnPhase.AutoPostPlay`, awaits `Hook.AfterAutoPostPlayPhaseEntered(...)` for every player, then at CombatManager.cs:1172-1175 flips each player to `PlayerTurnPhase.End`, and only at CombatManager.cs:1177-1180 fires `Hook.BeforeTurnEnd`. sts2_rl/combat.py:789 then :793 reproduces exactly that ordering as a STEP, not a listener, so it no longer depends on registration order. CloakClasp.cs:24-36 implements `BeforeSideTurnEnd` and reads `PileType.Hand.GetPile(base.Owner).Cards` at that moment; sts2_rl/relics/cloak_clasp.py:19-23 implements on_player_turn_end -- the sim's Hook.BeforeTurnEnd slot (hooks.py:498-501) -- and reads len(player.hand) there. Both C# AutoPostPlay implementers that the sim ports (StampedePower.cs:18 -> powers.py:1089; HowlFromBeyond.cs:32 -> cards/howl_from_beyond.py:45) now drain in the earlier phase, so the hand Cloak Clasp counts is the post-auto-play hand on both sides; executed, both give 3.  RECONCILED 2026-07-28 (Task 0, ledger-vs-code pass after the Tier 1 fix campaign): this entry was recorded `gap` against pre-campaign code and the divergence is closed today. The issue it replaced read: audit/records/seam/turn_structure.json guard G8 owns this mechanism and verdicts it a gap; cited and matched under binding rule 3. C# enters a dedicated AutoPostPlay phase strictly BEFORE Hook.BeforeTurnEnd (CombatManager.cs:1160-1176), so every end-of-turn auto-play has already resolved -- and already left the hand -- when Cloak Clasp counts cards. The sim has no such phase: StampedePower fires from on_player_turn_end (powers.py:1025), the same walk this relic is in, so the answer depends on listener order. The seam's executed evidence is again this relic's: 'with a 5-card hand and Stampede 2, forcing Stampede first gives 3 block (the C# answer), the natural relics-before-powers order gives 5'. The ported Howl From Beyond card (cards/howl_from_beyond.py:45) is the same shape. Recorded separately from G1 because they are different missing structures -- G1 is sub-phase ordering WITHIN BeforeTurnEnd, G2 is a whole phase BEFORE it -- and fixing either alone leaves the other.

The `player != base.Owner` / `card.Owner != base.Owner` / `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player (and, for the participants form, also admits pets). The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState) and models no pet creature, so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

guards.what: N2: the slot -- on_player_turn_end fires before the hand is discarded
guards.rationale: Load-bearing for a relic that counts the hand: BeforeSideTurnEnd precedes both EndOfTurnCleanup and FlushPlayerHand in C# (CombatManager.cs:1250-1255 and the flush that follows). The sim matches -- combat.py:654 fires on_player_turn_end, and only then come _process_turn_end_cards (:658) and `if self.hooks.should_flush_hand(): self.player.discard_hand()` (:662-663), with hooks.after_player_turn_end (the AfterTurnEnd slot, where relic/parrying_shield lives) after the flush. Confirmed by execution in `py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order`, which shows on_player_turn_end as the last player-turn event before the next turn's on_block_cleared. Rule 7: combat.py is not hashed here.

The BlockVar is 1, so the multiply is the identity and the truncating cast can never bite; no AscensionHelper call in the file. C#'s `if (cards.Count != 0)` maps to the sim's `if player.hand`, and both are redundant against a 0-block application -- kept on both sides. Read carefully because a BlockVar of 1 is exactly the kind of constant a port drops as 'obviously 1' and then cannot ascend later.
The same list. Notably NOT the pile-limbo case of PROMPT.md bug class 7: this fires between plays, so no card is sitting in PileType.Play.

guards.what: N5: `CreatureCmd.GainBlock(Owner.Creature, num, ValueProp.Unpowered, null)` (CloakClasp.cs:33) vs `BlockCmd.apply(..., props=ValueProp.UNPOWERED)` (cloak_clasp.py:22-24)
guards.rationale: Same prop, and it matters: BlockCmd.apply skips modify_block_additive/multiplicative unless is_powered_attack(props) (cmds.py:141-144), so Dexterity does not add to Cloak Clasp's block. Same handling as relic/captains_wheel N3 in this batch. The card source is null on both sides.
